confirmed.title: On a page with a shown original, a popup that takes focus right after a Sift click, or by select() or dialog.show(), still closes at once
confirmed.where: src/main/index.ts:215-221 (only HTMLElement.prototype.focus, and only while `clicking`); src/content/index.ts:3457-3463 (sift-click 'end' is sent right after proxy.click, before the page's microtasks, frames and timers run)
confirmed.evidence: Fixture /fx/r13int7-focusasync.html (with an iframe, so Sift shows a portal). Each button appends a share popup to <body>, focuses its first control and closes on focusout. In Sift: 'Share in a microtask' logged ['share open micro focus copyurl','share closed'], and the same for the frame and timeout variants. 'Share with the link selected' (input.select(), no focus() call) logged ['share open sel focus url','share closed']. 'Share in a dialog' (a non-modal <dialog> with show()) logged ['dialog open focus dcopy','dialog closed']. In all five, Sift's focus went back to the button pressed and no sheet showed. On the original each logged only '… open', with document.activeElement on the popup's control. Control case /fx/r13int7-focusasync-noportal.html (the same page without the iframe): all five stay open in Sift and show as a sheet, because <body> is inert there. Also seen: a clipboard.js copy on /fx/r12int-clipjs-portal.html leaves document.activeElement on its textarea during the copy, so select() really moves focus out of Sift on portal pages.
confirmed.repro: SIFT_PORT=9467 ./scripts/chrome.sh start; cd /tmp/claude-1001/-home-nico/aac11194-acaf-4dad-a334-0620115b1898/scratchpad/r13int7; FX=http://127.0.0.1:8799/fx/r13int7-focusasync.html SIFT_PORT=9467 SIFT_TAB=R2-interaction bun focusclose.ts sift 'Share in a microtask' (also 'Share in a frame', 'Share after a timeout', 'Share with the link selected', 'Share in a dialog'); the same with 'orig' in place of 'sift' for the original; FX=http://127.0.0.1:8799/fx/r13int7-focusasync-noportal.html for the control.
confirmed.suspectedCause: The F1200 guard is narrow. It fails only a synchronous HTMLElement.prototype.focus() inside proxy.click. React 18, Vue and Headless UI focus in a microtask, effect or frame after the event, and by then 'end' was sent. input.select() and dialog.show() focus natively without calling focus(). The new popup is not inert until the MutationObserver's refreshShield runs, which then blurs it. Lead: while Sift is shown, have the page-world helper treat any element that is not shownAt() and sits in a <body> child Sift has not shielded yet (neither data-sift-inert nor a portal ancestor) like an inert one, at all times rather than only during a click. Wrap select() (use setSelectionRange without focus there) and HTMLDialogElement.show() the same way. Or keep 'clicking' set until a timeout and a frame after the click.
confirmed.verdict: Confirmed; I would rate it medium to high. I used my copies of the reporter's scripts, port 9467, tab 'skeptic'. On /fx/r13int7-focusasync.html, focusclose.ts in Sift logged [... open, ... closed] for all five buttons: micro, frame, later, sel and dlg. Each time Sift's focus went back to the button pressed and no sheet showed (layer null). I reran micro, sel and dlg with a 4 s wait and got the same result. The open line itself names the popup's control ('focus copyurl', 'focus url', 'focus dcopy'). So focus really left Sift, and the popup closed when the shield made it inert. With Sift off, all five logged only '... open', with document.activeElement on #copyurl, #url or #dcopy. The control page without the iframe (r13int7-focusasync-noportal.html) kept all five open in Sift as a sheet with Sift's focus inside it. So the shown portal is the cause. The code matches. In src/main/index.ts:215-221 the guard wraps only HTMLElement.prototype.focus and only while clicking > 0. In src/content/index.ts the sift-click 'end' is sent in the finally right after proxy.click, so microtasks, frames and timers run after the flag is cleared. select() and dialog.show() focus natively, so they bypass the wrapper even during the click. Two of the five (sel and dlg) are synchronous inside the click, so they are squarely F1200's own case.
confirmed.fix: In src/main/index.ts, stop gating the focus guard on `clicking`. While Sift is shown, treat any connected target that is not shownAt() and sits outside the elements Sift exempts as inert: skip the native focus and dispatch sift-focus. Wrap HTMLInputElement/HTMLTextAreaElement.prototype.select (set the selection without focusing) and HTMLDialogElement.prototype.show the same way. A narrower option is to keep `clicking` set until a setTimeout(0) plus a requestAnimationFrame after 'end' in H.act (src/content/index.ts ~3457). That covers microtask and frame focus, but not a later timeout.

confirmed.title: A held submit on a '#' or 'javascript:' form runs the page's submit handler once a second (one Enter adds the item 8 times), delays a plain '#' form until 8 s after load, and never sends it while the page is still loading
confirmed.where: src/content/proxy.ts:593-616 (submit: the hold and its retry, which re-runs the whole submit) and src/content/proxy.ts:631-636 (holdsSubmit: any '#' or 'javascript:' form, until load plus 8 s, readyState only)
confirmed.evidence: Fixture /fx/r13int7-heldsubmit.html. Form 'Add an item' has action="javascript:void(0)" and a submit listener that appends the item without calling preventDefault, as such forms usually do because their action does nothing. In Sift, typing Milk and pressing Enter once, 1.8 s after load (load ended at 0.35 s), logged 'added Milk at 1768', then 2771, 3775, 4780, 5785, 6788, 7794 and 8798. That is 8 list entries. On the original the same Enter logged one entry. Each retry calls submit() again, which presses Enter in the field again, clicks the submit button again and fires change and search again. The hold catches each new submit event because the page never cancels it, until 8 s after load. Same fixture, a plain GET form with action='#' and no script (Sift shows it as the bar search): Enter at 1.9 s navigated to ?q=milk# only at about 8.3 s. On the original, navigation started at once. /fx/r13int7-heldsubmit-slow.html is the same page plus an image whose request never completes, so readyState stays 'interactive'. There the search was still not sent 30 s after Enter. The retry polls every 500 ms for as long as the page is not 'complete'.
confirmed.repro: cd /tmp/claude-1001/-home-nico/aac11194-acaf-4dad-a334-0620115b1898/scratchpad/r13int7; SIFT_PORT=9467 SIFT_TAB=R2-interaction bun drive.ts goto:http://127.0.0.1:8799/fx/r13int7-heldsubmit.html wait:1000 'sclick:input[type=text]' type:Milk press:Enter wait:13000 'eval:window.__log' → 8 'added Milk' entries; original: goto, press:Alt+Shift+S, 'oclick:#item' type:Milk press:Enter wait:5000 'eval:window.__log' → 1 entry (press Alt+Shift+S again after). Delay: goto the same, wait:800 netlog 'sclick:input[type=search]' type:milk press:Enter, then url every 2 s → NAV GET ...?q=milk# only about 6.4 s after Enter; with r13int7-heldsubmit-slow.html no navigation after 30 s.
confirmed.suspectedCause: news17's hold (F1235) applies to every form whose action starts with '#' or 'javascript:' while the page loads or within 8 s of load, with no upper bound while readyState is not 'complete'. Each retry replays the whole submit (key events, the default button's click, the submit event), so a page that handles the submit without cancelling it acts each time. Lead: hold only when the native submission would reload this document (action '#' or the current URL, not 'javascript:') and only while no page handler has acted. Retry the submission itself once, not the Enter and click with all their handlers. Cap the wait at a few seconds after DOMContentLoaded, not 'complete' plus 8 s, and show 'loading' on Sift's field while it waits.
confirmed.verdict: Confirmed (high), and a regression from round 12's F1235 hold (it appears in research/round13/round12-fixes.diff). On /fx/r13int7-heldsubmit.html, load ended at 185 ms. I typed Milk in Sift's 'item' field and pressed Enter at about 1.8 s. The log then had 8 entries: 'added Milk at 1762, 2764, 3781, 4785, 5786, 6788, 7796, 8797', and #items had 8 children. With Sift off, the same Enter logged one entry ('added Milk at 2271'). The plain GET form with action '#' (Sift's bar search, 'Show items with'): Enter at about 1.6 s in Sift navigated to ?q=milk# only between 7.6 s and 9.6 s. With Sift off, navigation started at once. On r13int7-heldsubmit-slow.html, readyState stayed 'interactive' in Sift and there was no navigation at 17.6 s or 32.6 s. With Sift off on the same slow page (readyState interactive), Enter navigated at once. The code matches. In src/content/proxy.ts submit(), the hold prevents every submit event the page has not cancelled. Its retry calls the whole submit() again, which replays the Enter key, the default button's click and the submit event. holdsSubmit stays true for any '#' or 'javascript:' action until loadEventEnd + 8000, and the retry re-polls every 500 ms for as long as readyState is not 'complete'.
confirmed.fix: In src/content/proxy.ts holdsSubmit/submit: never hold a 'javascript:' action, because the browser's submission does nothing there anyway. Hold a '#' form only if the page ran no handler (check with watchReaction-style detection, or that the field value was not consumed). On retry, call f.requestSubmit(submitter) once instead of submit() and do not re-hold it. Cap the wait at a few seconds after DOMContentLoaded rather than waiting for readyState 'complete'.

confirmed.title: F1218 regression: a byline or count line with a name ('Posted by Sam Rivers, 3 hours ago', 'Reuters, 5 min ago', 'Live: 12,400 watching') is now part of the Short version's cache key, so a revisit pays for a new model call and shows the full text until it comes

confirmed.evidence: In Chrome with the mock, fx/blog.html is a post whose article has 'Posted by Sam Rivers, 3 hours ago' as a paragraph. That line reaches the text sent to the model. Visit 1 made 1 condense call. A reload made 0. After the line became '4 hours ago', the revisit made 1 new call (condense=1), and the Short version was not shown until that call ended. I rebuilt the pre-round-12 onlyTicks offline (r13ai/tickcmp.ts). It returns true for 'Posted by Sam Rivers, 3 hours ago', 'By Jane Doe, 3 hours ago', 'Reuters, 5 min ago', 'Por Juan Pérez, hace 3 horas', 'Jane Doe 3 hours ago', 'Sports desk, updated 3 hours ago' and 'Live: 12,400 watching'. The current one returns false for all of them. So stableText changes every time the relative time or the count ticks, and reuseShort refuses too, because its textLines differ.
confirmed.repro: bun /tmp/claude-1001/-home-nico/aac11194-acaf-4dad-a334-0620115b1898/scratchpad/r13ai/stable2.ts prints 'differs' for 'By Jane Doe, 3 hours ago'→'4 hours ago' and the others. In Chrome: cp fx/blogA.html fx/blog.html; watch.ts blog.html 6, twice, which gives condense=1 then 0. Then cp fx/blogB.html fx/blog.html; watch.ts blog.html 6, which gives condense=1.
confirmed.suspectedCause: onlyTicks now treats a line as ticking only if, once its VOLATILE and TICK parts are removed, every word left is a label. A byline joined by a comma or a space keeps a name ('sam rivers', 'reuters', 'live') and counts as content. Possible lead: also split byline parts at ', ' before a VOLATILE part, or drop a short line whose VOLATILE part sits at its end after a name. Keep F1218's sentence cases ('drew 9 million viewers') as content.
confirmed.verdict: Confirmed. This is a medium regression from the F1218 fix. git diff 7bd95ba..ae0fe8f -- src/shared/ticks.ts shows that the VOLATILE shortcut was removed. I copied the round-11 onlyTicks and compared it with the current one. Old returns true and current returns false for 'Posted by Sam Rivers, 3 hours ago', 'By Jane Doe, 3 hours ago', 'Reuters, 5 min ago', 'Por Juan Pérez, hace 3 horas', 'Jane Doe 3 hours ago', 'Sports desk, updated 3 hours ago' and 'Live: 12,400 watching'. With the real stableText, the cache key changes when only the time in those lines changes. 'BBC · 3hrs ago', 'Jane Doe · 3 hours ago' and 'By Jane Doe | Updated 3 hours ago' still keep the same key. In Chrome 9469 with the mock, blogA gave condense=1 on the first visit, and the reload gave condense=0. After the line changed to '4 hours ago' (blogB), the revisit showed the full text at 1 s with condense=0 and no Short version. A new call followed (condense=1), and the Short version came at 3 s. So an article with a comma-joined byline and a relative time pays for a new call on almost every revisit. F1218's sentence case ('The final drew 9 million viewers.') is still treated as content, as intended.
confirmed.fix: In src/shared/ticks.ts onlyTicks, also split byline parts at a comma or colon followed by a space: add `[,:]\s+` to PART. The existing check `parts.some(p => VOLATILE.test(p) && labelOnly(p))` then accepts 'Reuters, 5 min ago' and 'Posted by Sam Rivers, 3 hours ago'. A sentence like 'The final drew 9 million viewers, a record.' stays content, because its VOLATILE part is not label-only.

confirmed.title: A one-day 'no Short version' marker (and a one-day keep-title) is saved again for 7 days when the page turns out to be signed in after it asked
confirmed.where: src/background/index.ts:797 (`if (hit && !ttlOf(req, pc)) pc.saved.set(key, hit)` runs for a NO_SHORT hit too), :528 (the same for KEEP_TITLE hits), :974 (the 'private' task re-saves every pc.saved entry with PRIVATE_TTL)
confirmed.evidence: In Chrome with the mock, fx/latepriv.html is an article whose header gets a 'Sign out' link 4 s after load, and the mock answer is the full text, so the result is 'not much shorter'. Visit 1, before the link appears, stored '\u0000no-short' with exp 1d, as intended ('kept for a day at most, whichever model wrote it'). On visit 2 the request hit that marker and the page then turned private. IndexedDB now holds '\u0000no-short' with exp 7d, written fresh. That article gets no Short version for a week instead of a day. KEEP_TITLE hits take the same path: F1231 made them last a day, and here they become 7 days.
confirmed.repro: Run r13ai/mock.ts and r13ai/settings.ts mock. Run r13ai/watch.ts latepriv.html 3, then r13ai/idb.ts | grep no-short (exp 1d). Run r13ai/watch.ts latepriv.html 8, then r13ai/idb.ts | grep no-short (exp 7d).
confirmed.suspectedCause: pc.saved remembers every hit so that it can shorten its lifetime later. Markers that already expire in a day or 6 hours are re-saved with the 7-day private TTL, which lengthens their lifetime instead. Possible lead: never put NO_SHORT or KEEP_TITLE hits in pc.saved, or re-save with min(remaining, PRIVATE_TTL).
confirmed.verdict: Confirmed, medium. In code, both cache-hit paths call pc.saved.set for any hit: index.ts:797 (condense, NO_SHORT included) and :528 (lines, KEEP_TITLE included). When the page turns private, the 'private' task at :974 re-saves every pc.saved entry with cacheSet(key, v, PRIVATE_TTL), which gives a fresh 7-day expiry. In Chrome 9469 with the mock, visit 1 to fx/latepriv.html (checked at 3 s, before 'Sign out' appears at 4 s) stored '\u0000no-short' with exp 1d. Visit 2 (8 s) hit the marker, and the page turned private. IndexedDB then held '\u0000no-short' with exp 7d and a new ts. A third visit renewed it again (ts moved, still 7d). So each revisit within the week extends the block, which is worse than the claim says. I checked the KEEP_TITLE path by reading the code only: it follows the same pattern at :528.
confirmed.fix: In src/background/index.ts, do not put marker hits in pc.saved. At :797, use `if (hit && hit !== NO_SHORT && !ttlOf(req, pc))`. At :528, do the same with `hit !== KEEP_TITLE`. Another option: in the 'private' handler (:974), skip v === NO_SHORT || v === KEEP_TITLE.

confirmed.title: Usage report retried without limit: while sift.pujia.ar/e fails, Sift sends the same day's report again about every 2 s of browsing, not 'one anonymous request per day of use'
confirmed.where: src/background/stats.ts:37 and :52 (every bump schedules save(), which calls flushStats()) and :71-84 (a non-ok status leaves sent[day] unset, so the next save sends again; nothing backs off)
confirmed.evidence: Offline harness with a fake chrome.storage and fetch (r13ai/statsretry.ts) runs 20 bumps 2.1 s apart. With the endpoint answering 503, stats.ts sent 20 GET reports for the same past day in about 42 s and never set sent. With 204 it sent 1. Every active user would send a request every few seconds for as long as the endpoint is down or returns 404. That contradicts README.md:51 and site/index.html:48 ('one anonymous request/report per day of use') and puts load on the owner's server just when it is failing.
confirmed.repro: timeout 120 bun /tmp/claude-1001/-home-nico/aac11194-acaf-4dad-a334-0620115b1898/scratchpad/r13ai/statsretry.ts 503 prints '20 report requests'. With argument 204 it prints 1.
confirmed.suspectedCause: flushStats runs after every saved bump, with no record of when it last tried. Possible lead: remember the last attempt per day in storage, and retry at most every few hours, or on worker startup only, as onStartup already does.
confirmed.verdict: Confirmed, medium at the low end. In src/background/stats.ts, every bump schedules save() after 2 s, and save() always calls flushStats(). When the request gets a non-ok status (:76), sent[day] stays unset. When fetch throws (:80), the loop breaks, and nothing records the attempt. Nothing backs off. I ran the reporter's fake-chrome harness with 8 bumps 2.1 s apart, all four runs side by side. The endpoint answering 503, 404 or nothing at all got 8 report requests each for the one past day, with sent={}. With 204 it got 1 request, and sent was set. So while sift.pujia.ar/e is down or returns 404, every active user sends about one request per page view, with no limit. That breaks the README's 'one anonymous request per day of use'. The same-id retry the README mentions does not cover a retry on every bump.
confirmed.fix: In src/background/stats.ts, store the last attempt time (for example `tried[day]` or one `lastTry` timestamp in chrome.storage.local). flushStats should skip a day it tried within the last few hours. Another option: call flushStats from save() only when today() changed since the last call, and leave retries to onStartup and onInstalled.

R2-interaction: src/content/proxy.ts:593: while a submit is held (Corriere: from 4 to 20 s on a loaded machine), Sift's search field shows nothing, so a user pressing Enter early sees no sign that the search will run.
R2-interaction: src/content/proxy.ts:594: every submit() starts with clearTimeout(heldSubmit), so submitting any other form cancels a held submit of a different form without a word.

R2-interaction: src/content/index.ts:3457: sift-click is a plain CustomEvent on document, so page listeners on window in the capture phase see it before the page-world helper stops it (the same is true of sift-enter and sift-key).

R2-interaction: src/main/index.ts:85-103: switching to the original while a Sift search field is entered sends no sift-leave, so document.activeElement names the page field while focus is on Sift's switch, until the user clicks into the page.

R1-extractor: src/content/extract/generic.ts:2588 groupName copies every child of the fieldset (Array.from(g.children).find) for each field, so it is quadratic: 2000 radios in one fieldset take 1.6 s per look, 4000 take 6.4 s (CPU profile: 1.2 s of 1.9 s in groupName). ':scope > legend' or a per-pass cache fixes it.

R1-extractor: src/content/extract/generic.ts:7311 findDialog still saves a cut look's partial visited set and blocks as shownLast (next look's shownPrev), while extractAll guards only lastShown/lastBars on a cut. A popup check in the look right after a cut compares against a partial page view.

R1-extractor: src/content/dom.ts:715 sameWordsAsPeer checks only the group's first 60 inputs, so a radio past the 60th never finds its twin. With no fieldset or form, it runs querySelectorAll over the whole document.body for each label.

R1-extractor: src/content/extract/generic.ts:5934 the arXiv listing alternates entry by entry between facts rows and loose bold-plus-paragraph blocks (the dd 'blocky' cutoff is tlen > 250), so similar entries look different.

R1-extractor: src/content/extract/generic.ts:4282 and other getBoundingClientRect reads: pages built from content-visibility:auto sections pay the same first-look layout cost (2000 sections: 7 s first look, 0.4-0.6 s after). Reordering scrollBox does not help there.
